text:
sam_sales: Quick question — running into a presales POC with a fintech customer. They're trying to do streaming SSE with function/tool-calling and get structured JSON outputs. Handshake sometimes fails on token refresh and the client sees 403 mid-stream. Any quick checklist?

ira_engineer: Hey Sam — couple things to verify: 1) are they using ephemeral creds or long-lived API key? 2) which sdk (js/go/python) and which transport (native websocket vs SSE)?

sam_sales: They're on the JS SDK (browser embed for demo) + SSE fallback. Using short-lived credentials via our demo token rotation flow.

devon_se: Browser + SSE + short-lived creds is fiddly. Browser clients need a stable refresh endpoint. If the streaming connection outlives the token TTL and you try to refresh mid-stream the server will reject. For demo we recommend either: 1) use proxy server that mints ephemeral tokens and rotates them on reconnects, or 2) use our websocket SDK which supports in-band reconnects.

jen_ops: Also check CORS + preflight. SSE endpoints must allow the demo origin and include the right Allow-Credentials header if they're using cookies.

sam_sales: Got it. Customer asked whether function-calling (tool calls) are supported in streaming mode with structured JSON batches. They want tool outputs emitted as separate events.

ira_engineer: Yes — we stream incremental chunks, and function/tool outputs come as structured events. Example (SSE):

```
event: token
data: {"type":"tool_call_start","tool":"account_lookup","call_id":"abc123"}

event: message
data: {"type":"token","role":"assistant","content":"..."}

event: tool
data: {"type":"tool_call_result","call_id":"abc123","payload":{"status":"ok","account_id":42}}
```

ira_engineer: Consumers should watch for the `tool` event and parse JSON per-line. Recommend using our SDK's onTool callback to normalize across transports.

devon_se: If they need strict JSON array at the end, we can add a `final` event with the assembled structure. But that's an extra layer — easier to consume per-event.

sam_sales: They're worried about pricing — streaming vs non-streaming cost model and whether tool calls count as tokens.

jen_ops: Streaming generation uses the same per-token billing as non-streamed. Tool calls: tokens consumed by the model are billed; outbound tool invocation (e.g., external API calls) is not billed by Redwood. If they use Redwood-managed toolchain (like file search via our embeddings), embeddings calls are billed separately.

sam_sales: Cool. They also raised security: can we attest SOC2 + bring-your-own-KMS? Also need IP allowlist and SAML SSO for admin console.

devon_se: Yes, SOC2 is in our compliance pack. BYOK/KMS is available for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted customers we offer KMS integration via customer-managed keys in supported cloud regions (we'll need a support ticket). IP allowlist and SAML SSO are available for enterprise plans — require SAML metadata and the admin email list.

sam_sales: Any immediate blockers for the POC?

ira_engineer: Potential blockers:
- Browser SSE + ephemeral tokens (reconnect logic missing)
- CORS + cookies flags
- If they want BYOK and are on hosted tier we need legal + infra change (slow)
- If they require on-prem-only routing, that'll push to Private deployment (longer lead)

jen_ops: Ops note: If they plan for high QPS during demo, enable burst override on the Dedicated trial or the hosted burst quota. Otherwise they'll see throttling.

sam_sales: TL;DR — what's our recommended short-term plan to unblock demo this week?

devon_se: 1) Switch demo to websocket SDK for stable reconnection. 2) Proxy token refresh through a tiny lambda that returns fresh ephemeral keys and triggers client reconnect when TTL < 30s. 3) Use onTool callback to parse tool events. 4) If they insist on BYOK, escalate to account exec — not doable before demo.

ira_engineer: I'll paste a tiny code snippet for the client reconnect logic: 

```js
// pseudo: reconnect when token close to expiry
async function startStream() {
  let token = await fetch('/mint-token').then(r=>r.text());
  const ws = new WebSocket(`wss://api.redwood.ai/stream?token=${token}`);
  ws.onmessage = (ev)=> handleEvent(JSON.parse(ev.data));
  ws.onclose = async ()=> {
    // immediate reconnect + new token 
    setTimeout(startStream, 500);
  };
}
startStream();
```

sam_sales: Perfect. Can someone own the demo checklist and be in the call with the customer Thursday 10am PST?

devon_se: I can join. I'll own the SDK bits.

jen_ops: I'll cover ops + pricing and add notes about burst capacity.

ira_engineer: I'll handle token flow and sample proxy.

sam_sales: Awesome — I'll send calendar invite and put together the POC checklist. Also adding a quick pre-demo run at Wednesday 2pm PT.

deploy-bot: New support ticket created: #SUP-4821 referencing ephemeral token rotation for presales POC. Assigned: ira_engineer, devon_se.

sam_sales: Thanks all. Leaving notes for handoff to AE after demo: they want official pricing for 1M tokens/month streaming + Dedicated trial (2 GPUs) and formal security questionnaire.

devon_se: Noted. We'll compile a minimal runbook for the demo flow and sample code snippets in the handoff doc.

jen_ops: I'll start the security questionnaire draft (answers for SOC2/BYOK/SAML/IP allowlist).

sam_sales: <@devon_se> <@ira_engineer> <@jen_ops> appreciate it. If anything blocks before Wed 2pm ping here. :thumbsup:
